skills/dependency-audit.description: Audit a project's npm dependencies for known vulnerabilities and risky install scripts before installing, upgrading, or shipping. Use when the user pastes or attaches a package.json/lockfile, lists dependencies, or asks to check/audit/scan their packages for security issues — including comparing two snapshots (a PR diff) or checking license compliance.
skills/dependency-audit.he: תבחן npm תלויות של פרויקט עבור נקודות תורפה ידועות ותסריטים מתקינים מסוכנים לפני התקנת, שדרוג, או משלוח. השתמש בעת הדבקות המשתמש או מחבר חבילה. json/ loockfile, רשימות תלויות, או מבקש לבדוק/אודיט/סריקה את חבילותיהם עבור בעיות אבטחה, כולל השוואת שתי תמונות (התקן PR) או בדיקת ציות לרשיון.

skills/incident-response.description: Turn a flagged npm supply-chain finding — or just a vague, non-technical description of one ("this package looks sketchy," "someone said we got hacked," "npm install did something weird") — into concrete remediation steps. Use whenever the user wants to know what to actually do about a suspicious/compromised/flagged package, however precisely or vaguely they describe it — not for the initial trust/vulnerability investigation itself (see package-trust-check/dependency-audit for that).

Use when the user asks if a single named package is safe, compromised, hijacked, suspicious, or "can I trust this" — not for auditing a full package.json/lockfile (see dependency-audit) and not for a plain factual question like "what does X do."
